one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes a triple-tribute column in three sections: boxing (Manny), Comelec (Andy and Bing), and Customs (Bert). FULL DISCLOSURE: CJP is not a diehard boxing fan -- he sees boxing as brutal combat reminiscent of the gladiators who duelled to death for the ghoulish entertainment of the Romans; with due respect to Manny Pacquiao's grandiose claim that he boxes 'for the Filipino,' the grim reality in any professional boxing bout is 'money,' as Floyd Mayweather Jr. unabashedly proclaims. CJP expected at least that the promoters and combatants would be fair to fans who paid handsomely (ringside or pay-per-view) and to those who bet hard-earned dollars and pesos. Complete disclosure should be the unbroken rule. Pacquiao and his handlers were unfair for not revealing his injured shoulder on time -- no wonder he faces Nevada sanctions and suits from irate fans and bettors. Fortunately for him, a PH suit may not prosper because gambling is banned here except for those specifically allowed by law (horse racing on specific days in specific tracks, Pagcor outlets including Solaire and City of Dreams, sweepstakes lotteries). Pacquiao's non-disclosure is undisputed; he answered 'No' to the box in the official questionnaire asking about any 'injury to [his] shoulders, elbows or hands.' Speculation: disclosure may have meant postponement or cancellation, meaning no or reduced money. CJP believes Pacquiao should have accepted his defeat graciously -- that would have been most honorable. True, Mayweather just danced his way to victory, a disgusting strategy but allowed by Nevada rules; Pacquiao accepted the rules along with the grand rewards Nevada secures for boxing, gambling, howling, and hype. It is said that no Filipino loses an election -- either he wins or is cheated; must it be the same in boxing? Banter aside, fairness, honor, and transparency should define every public endeavor, including boxing. COMELEC APPOINTEES: Kudos to Dean Andres D. Bautista, new Comelec chair. At only 51, Andy brings freshness, vigor, probity, and integrity to the poll body a year before the May 2016 presidential election. He has pedigreed credentials worthy even of an SC seat -- class valedictorian of Ateneo Law, bar topnotcher, Harvard LLM, FEU law dean, Philippine Judicial Academy lecturer, Philippine Association of Law Schools chair, and among the 10 original holders of the 'Chief Justice Panganiban Professorial Chairs on Liberty and Prosperity.' He practiced law in PH and abroad and, while still a law student, clerked for then-CJ Marcelo B. Fernan. Though his expertise is constitutional and commercial law, he studied election law as a PPCRV trustee. His vast managerial experience -- chief executive of several large firms, PCGG chair -- will help him steer the giant Comelec bureaucracy. The President could not have chosen a better Comelec chief. Congratulations also to new Comelec Commissioner Rowena V. Guanzon. Strong-willed and fiercely independent, Bing has a formidable background: litigation lawyer with a string of landmark victories, book writer, law professor, UP Law dean's lister, Harvard MPA, well-regarded in the legal community (including the SC) for her gender-equality advocacy. Armed with practical experience in rough-and-tumble politics as former Cadiz City mayor, she mirrors the feistiness, bravado, and wit of former Comelec commissioner Heidi Yorac. CJP expects her to team up well with Chairman Andy to assure free, honest, credible 2016 elections. CUSTOMS BOSS: CJP also welcomes the appointment of Customs Commissioner Alberto D. Lina. He has known Bert for over 40 years since he was a lowly clerk at the auditing firm of L.C. Diaz and Associates, and tracked his rise as an innovative, driven, self-made entrepreneur. CJP has no doubt Lina's acceptance was motivated solely by his desire to serve the country. He rejects unverified media reports that Lina took the job to promote the financial interest of his multibillion-peso logistics business -- if all he wanted were a few more billion pesos, he could just list his business on the PSE and presto, the market value of his wealth would multiply several times. His willingness to divest from companies doing business with BoC speaks well of his patriotism. Let's give him a chance to prove his worth and show how his grit, integrity, and skill can transform the most graft-prone office in our government.
